s.t:
Work across the full Linux stack from kernel through GUI to optimise Ubuntu, the world’s most widely used Linux desktop and server, for the latest silicon.
The role is a fast-paced, problem-solving role that’s challenging yet very exciting. The right candidate must be resourceful, articulate, and able to deliver on a wide variety of solutions across PC and IoT technologies. Our teams partner with specialist engineers from major silicon companies to integrate next-generation features and performance enhancements for upcoming hardware.
Location: This is a Globally remote role

s.h: What your day will look like
s.t:
Design and implement the best Ubuntu integration for the latest IoT and server-class hardware platforms and software stacks
Work with partners to deliver a delightful, optimised, first class Ubuntu experience on their platforms
Take a holistic approach to the Ubuntu experience on partner platforms with inputs on technical plans, testing strategy, quality metrics
Participate as technical lead on complex customer engagements involving complete system architectures from cloud to edge
Help our customers integrate their apps, SDKs, build device OS images, optimize applications with Ubuntu Core, Desktop and Server
Work with the most advanced operating systems and application technologies available in the enterprise world.
Joining Canonical , you will partner with bright minds from all over the world, and work with an exciting set of new technologies in a fast growing company with a truly unique and ambitious vision to build a better platform with free software. You will work with customers on exciting IoT and server platforms and technologies, built to support different verticals: from robots to data centers, from telco to retail.

s.h: What we are looking for in you
s.t:
You love technology and working with brilliant people
You have a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, STEM or similar
You have experience with Linux packaging (Debian, RPM, Yocto)
You have experience working with open source communities and licences
You have experience working with C, C++
You can work in a globally distributed team through self-discipline and self-motivation.
Additional skills that you might also bring
Experience with graphics stacks
Good understanding of networking - TCP/IP, DHCP, HTTP/REST
Basic understanding of security best practices in IoT or server environments
Good communication skills, ideally public speaking experience
IoT / Embedded experience – from board and SoC, BMCs, bootloaders and firmware to OS, through apps and services
Some experience with Docker/OCI containers/K8s

About Canonical
Canonical is a pioneering tech firm that is at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open source projects and the platform for AI, IoT and the cloud, we are changing the world on a daily basis. We recruit on a global basis and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence - in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do.
Canonical has been a remote-first company since its inception in 2004.​ Work at Canonical is a step into the future, and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game. Canonical provides a unique window into the world of 21st-century digital business.
Canonical is an equal opportunity employer
We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products. Whatever your identity, we will give your application fair consideration.

Semiconductor Systems Engineer – Remote Bright Vision Technologies is a technology consulting and software development company delivering cloud, AI, data, and enterprise solutions across the United States. This is a fantastic opportunity to join an established and well-respected organization offering tremendous career growth potential.

Job Title: Semiconductor Systems Engineer Location: 100% Remote (U.S.) Position Type: Full-time, Direct W2 Salary Range: $100,000–$150,000 Annually Experience Required: 6+ years Sponsorship: U.S. Citizens, Green Card Holders, EAD Holders, and H-1B transfer candidates are encouraged to apply.

We are unable to sponsor new H-1B visa petitions for this position. Job Summary We are seeking an experienced Semiconductor Software Engineer to design and build software tooling, firmware, and infrastructure that support semiconductor design, verification, manufacturing, and post-silicon validation.

In this role you will partner with hardware engineers and EDA teams to build software that accelerates silicon development cycles and improves yield, performance, and quality.

The ideal candidate will combine strong software engineering fundamentals with practical experience working alongside hardware teams in EDA, verification, or post-silicon environments.

In this role you will work closely with cross-functional partners — product, design, engineering, operations, and business stakeholders — to translate ambiguous requirements into well-engineered solutions, and will be expected to raise the bar through code review, design review, and mentorship of more junior engineers.

The successful candidate brings strong engineering discipline, a clear communication style, and a track record of shipping meaningful work that holds up well in production. Key Responsibilities Design and build software tooling that accelerates semiconductor design and verification workflows.

Develop firmware and low-level software interacting directly with silicon, including drivers and BSPs. Build infrastructure to support large-scale EDA tool execution on compute farms and cloud platforms.

Develop post-silicon validation tooling, including high-throughput test orchestration, programmable stimulus generation, and result aggregation systems that scale across many parts and many test environments. Build data pipelines for design, verification, and characterization data, supporting downstream analytics and ML.

Implement debug tooling and diagnostic infrastructure for hardware bring-up and silicon characterization, giving engineers fast feedback loops on the silicon-software interface during critical validation windows. Partner with hardware engineers to translate hardware-specific requirements into clean software designs.

Optimize software for performance and scalability in compute-intensive semiconductor workflows. Lead architecture and code reviews that span the software-hardware boundary, ensuring that abstractions, interfaces, and constraints between the two domains are well-understood and respected across the team.

Contribute to internal libraries and tooling shared across silicon design teams.

Maintain comprehensive, current technical documentation — including architecture diagrams, design decisions, configuration references, runbooks, and operational procedures — so that the system remains supportable, auditable, and easy to onboard new engineers onto over time.

Mentor and coach junior and mid-level engineers through code review, design review, pair programming, and structured knowledge sharing, helping the broader team grow in technical maturity and confidence over time.

Continuously evaluate emerging hardware platforms and toolchains, assessing maturity, fit for purpose, and total cost of ownership, and make grounded recommendations on which to adopt, pilot, or defer based on real engineering needs.

Required Qualifications Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field. Six or more years of software engineering experience, with significant time in semiconductor environments. Strong programming skills in C, C++, and Python.

Hands-on experience with EDA, verification, or post-silicon validation workflows. Solid understanding of hardware-software interaction at a low level. Experience building large-scale compute infrastructure (grid, cloud, HPC). Strong scripting and automation skills. Experience with data pipelines for design or characterization data.

Excellent debugging and troubleshooting skills. Strong communication and documentation skills. Preferred Qualifications Exposure to SystemVerilog or other HDLs. Familiarity with UVM-based verification workflows. Experience with cloud-based EDA workflows. Hands-on experience with ML applied to silicon design. Advanced degree in EE or related field.

Job Summary: In this role, you will supervise a team of Control Systems personnel, estimate project staffing needs, and schedule and assign work. You will prepare discipline estimates and work plans and review and approve control systems investigations and studies.

Your leadership will drive high quality work plans, successful implementation of control system components, team support and training, and project performance. This position is designated as part-time telework per our global telework policy and will require at least three days of in-person attendance per week at the assigned office or project.

Weekly in-person schedules will be determined by the individual and their supervisor, in consultation with functional or project leadership. #LI-AM3 Major Responsibilities: Plans, develops, directs, and participates in the day-to-day Control Systems engineering activity on small to medium sized projects or a portion of a major project with minimal to moderate complexity within a global business unit utilizing relevant Engineering Department Procedures (EDPs), design standards and guides, and Bechtel Standard Application Programs (BSAPs).

Supervises, coordinates, and reviews the work of personnel assigned, estimates staffing needs, and schedules and assigns work accordingly. Provides the technical input to meet procurement requirements.

Prepares or oversees the preparation of Control Systems discipline estimates and work plans in accordance with project scope, schedule, and budget, and manages implementation and performance accordingly. Reviews and makes recommendations for the Control Systems engineering aspects of bid evaluations and awards for approval by project engineering.

When directed, coordinates with client representatives to obtain their approval of Control Systems engineering aspects of the work. Reviews and approves key calculations, licensing evaluations, design documents, supplier drawings and data, material specifications, drawings, and change orders, for the project to which assigned.

Ensures that assigned Control Systems engineering personnel receive appropriate on-the-job training for their professional development. Assists in the preparation and reviews of project procedures and cost estimates for proposals, forecasts, and change orders.

Education and Experience Requirements: Requires bachelor's degree (or international equivalent) and 8 -10 years of relevant experience or 12-14 years of relevant work experience Required Knowledge and Skills: Knowledge of instrumentation and control valves including specifications, generation of data sheets, application of tubing, and instrument installations.

Knowledge of control system design including digital and analog control logic, control system network architecture, allocation of facility control system I/O, graphic displays, and acceptance tests.

Demonstrated strong frontline leadership skills and emphasis on continuous improvement and team building and an ability to cope with conflicting deadlines, frequent interruptions, and multiple tasks. Ability to facilitate technical discussions with third parties (e.g., clients, suppliers, regulators).

Prior experience in planning and executing greenfield or brownfield projects in semiconductor, data center and life sciences market segments. As a Senior Systems Engineer I, you will own the hardware lifecycle for RF-based counter-drone detection systems, working across engineering, manufacturing, quality, and certification. You will also contribute to early technical decisions such as concept definition and component selection.

Own the end-to-end lifecycle of RF sensor hardware, from early prototypes through production ramp and sustaining support.

Degree in Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a related field.
Experience owning hardware products across the lifecycle, ideally including manufacturing introduction and sustaining engineering.
Solid systems-level understanding of RF products, with hands-on validation and troubleshooting skills.
Experience supporting concept development and making pragmatic component choices for production-ready hardware.
Exposure to regulatory compliance and certification processes (e.g., RED/FCC) is a strong plus.
Strong cross-functional communication skills and a practical, solution-oriented mindset.

Join Quantum-Systems and help bring autonomous ground systems into real-world operations. As Senior Payload Integration Engineer, you will own the payload integration across our UGV platforms: the electrical, electronic, and mechanical integration of a wide range of mission payloads into our own Mandrill UGV and partner vehicle platforms.

Your goal is a payload-agnostic platform with scalable, reusable interfaces instead of one-off solutions, so we can adapt quickly to evolving mission needs without redesigning the vehicle for every new configuration.
This is a senior individual contributor role with real ownership. You drive the integration architecture end to end, from interface definition through bring-up and commissioning to the point where the complete E/E system is proven to work on the vehicle. You will work at the intersection of vehicle hardware, autonomy and MOSAIC orchestration software, mechanical engineering, suppliers, and manufacturing.

s.h: What is your Day to Day Mission
s.t:
Payload Integration Architecture and Ownership
Define and own the electrical, electronic, and mechanical integration concept for various payloads across our UGV platforms, ensuring scalable and reusable interfaces instead of one-off solutions.
Design, specify, and validate payload interfaces: power supply, signal routing, communication interfaces, connectors, mounting concepts, cooling, grounding and shielding, and serviceability.
Enable a payload-flexible vehicle platform that supports a wide range of customer-specific payloads (power profiles, environmental conditions, data interfaces) without major redesigns for every new configuration.
Electrical, Electronic and mechanical Integration
Integrate payloads into the vehicle power, network, compute, and control architectures: schematics, harnessing, connectors, fusing, diagnostics, and interface documentation.
Work with vehicle communication buses (CAN, automotive Ethernet) to bring payload data and control interfaces cleanly into the vehicle architecture.
Own the health of the complete E/E system: systematic cross-domain troubleshooting across payload, harness, power, compute, and software.
Drive payload mounting together with internal vehicle teams and external suppliers: brackets, packaging, accessibility, vibration robustness, environmental protection, maintainability, and manufacturability.
Bring-up, Commissioning and Validation
Plan and execute payload bring-up and commissioning on vehicle prototypes and demonstrators: mechanical fitment, electrical integration, software provisioning (flashing, configuration, diagnostics), troubleshooting, and validation up to full system commissioning where the complete E/E system is proven to work.
Define acceptance criteria, build and run system-level test setups, automate recurring integration and regression tests with scripts and test tooling, and support field testing.
Translate integration findings into design improvements for vehicle and payload interfaces, and feed validated test workflows into our CI and test infrastructure together with the HW integration and SW Factory teams.
Work directly with payload suppliers: clarify requirements, review technical documentation, align interface specifications, and drive issue resolution.
Cross-Functional Collaboration and Documentation
Create clear interface control documents, integration guides, test reports, lessons learned, and reusable standards for future payload integrations.
Actively support build-ups, rework, payload installation, and vehicle-level commissioning in the workshop during prototype and customer-specific integration phases.

s.h: What you bring to the team
s.t:
Engineering degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics, vehicle systems, or a comparable technical field.
5+ years of hands-on experience in field robotics, vehicle, or mechatronic system integration; you have brought complex E/E systems to life on real vehicles or machines.
Strong E/E integration expertise: power distribution, signal interfaces, connectors, wiring harnesses, grounding, shielding, diagnostics, and vehicle-level troubleshooting.
Hands-on experience with vehicle communication buses (CAN, ideally CAN-FD or automotive Ethernet), including reading and debugging bus traffic during integration.
Solid mechanical integration understanding: mounting concepts, packaging, tolerances, vibration, environmental robustness, accessibility, and serviceability.
Practical software skills for integration work: Linux, scripting (e.g. Python or Bash), software provisioning and configuration of embedded devices, and issue tracking tools. You are comfortable automating recurring integration tests.
Experience defining and running validation setups from bench and rig level up to vehicle-level testing, with a quality-first mindset and the discipline to design reliable, repeatable test setups.
Strong integration mindset: systematic in debugging, structured in documentation, and able to turn unclear payload requirements into practical engineering solutions.
Hands-on mentality: comfortable working directly on vehicles, prototypes, harnesses, brackets, and payload installations in the workshop.
Strong communication skills across engineering teams, suppliers, procurement, and program stakeholders.
Fluent in German and English.
High ownership, pragmatic, and thriving in a fast-paced environment.

Direct impact: See your contributions rapidly integrated from cutting-edge research into industrialized products, flying in the field within short development cycles.
Culture & Environment: A dynamic, fast-paced, and collaborative startup environment with flat hierarchies, efficient collaboration, and a strong emphasis on continuous learning opportunities.

Here at The Exploration Company, we are developing, producing, and operating Nyx, a modular and reusable space orbital vehicle that can eventually be refuelled in orbit and that can carry cargo - and potentially humans in the longer run.
The System Integration Senior Engineer will help lead the Nyx system end‑to‑end integration and verification, with a focus on functional platforms (Software in the Loop Platform, Processor in the Loop Platform, Hardware in the Loop Platform, Functional Simulation Facility).

You will define and execute test plans, manage requirement traceability, analyse test results, and close verification evidence across SIL/PIL/HIL and physical test campaigns.

Working closely with subsystem leads, AIT teams, and external partners, you will identify integration risks, resolve anomalies, and ensure that all mechanical functions perform safely and reliably throughout the mission profile.

This position requires a rigorous systems mindset, strong understanding of mechanical behaviour in the space environment, and the ability to lead multidisciplinary verification activities to successful closure.

In your capacity a System Integration Senior Engineer, your role will continuously evolve, but initially your day-to-day duties will include:
Ensure the definition and implementation of the Nyx Earth system integration and verification activities, which meets technical and programmatic requirements and considers the adequacy of model philosophy, facilities availability, planning and costing.
Define plans and specifications with clear Success Criteria and support the generation of test procedures with the Functional Platform team.
Drive the technical discussions, preparation, organization and execution of the system verification campaigns, to ensure the closure of all system verification aspects, including nominal and off nominal spacecraft behaviors.
Organise the different reviews for incremental progress and ultimate closure of verification events.
Generate reports and drive the closure of the Items for Verification and Validation covered by the campaign.
Collaborate with all Functional Chain responsible and engineering disciplines to prepare and perform the system activities.
Process the anomalies occurring during the verification campaign in coordination with the Product Assurance Team and the rest of the Engineering Team.

Master’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, or another related field.
5 to 10 years of experience in systems design, analysis, and testing of aerospace or space-related systems, with a focus on integration of complex spacecraft and/or testing activities.
Hands-on hardware experience.
Practical experience / contact with functional test platforms, such as software in the loop, hardware in the loop, and bench testing.
Experience in the development and verification of space hardware.
Spacecraft systems knowledge.

Strong oral and written communication skills
Strong analysis and problem-solving skills
Strong organizing and prioritization of tasks
Positive and flexible attitude to get the job done
Ability to communicate at all levels of the business

Space enthusiast: ready to change the European space industry
Ability to thrive in a high paced development environment

Where Europe's enterprises adopt AI
Langdock is the AI platform used by more than 10,000 companies to give employees secure access to the leading AI models, to build and share agents and to automate repetitive workflows. We have grown past $40M ARR while remaining a small team, and we care deeply about operating efficiently across the entire company.
For many enterprises, Langdock is becoming the place where most of the net-new work is produced. As people and agents create more documents, analyses, decisions, and automations inside AI interfaces, the context and data behind that work accumulate within Langdock. This gives us the opportunity to earn a larger role in their technology stack by building a platform they choose to rely on.
Our ambition is to build that platform for European enterprises while preserving their control over data, model providers, and deployment environments. We have made meaningful progress at the application layer, but much of the foundation beneath it still needs to be built.
You can watch the Meet the engineering team video to get a feeling for how we work.

Systems Engineers solve our most complex technical problems inside and across Langdock's shared services when existing building blocks or standard architectures are insufficient. These are problems where correctness under failure, performance, scale, security, and cost interact.
This is a project-oriented role rather than ownership of one permanent layer. You might spend a period on distributed execution, then move into storage architecture, workload isolation, or model serving as company priorities change. The constant is sustained investigation of unfamiliar systems and responsibility for turning that understanding into a production system.
Systems Engineers own the difficult mechanism and the measurable improvement it creates, whether in correctness, capability, performance, reliability, or cost. They operate what they build, while the Platform owner remains accountable for the service contract and long-term lifecycle around it.
What you might work on

Distributed state and execution. Design systems that remain correct when work is concurrent, long-running, retried, resumed, or moved between processes. Define explicit invariants for ordering, idempotency, recovery, and tenant isolation.
Storage and data systems. Improve how large volumes of customer and agent-generated data are stored, versioned, moved, and recovered while preserving consistency, data residency, and predictable performance.
Secure compute for agents. Develop the isolation, runtime, and scheduling mechanisms behind a shared sandbox service for untrusted code. The system needs persistent filesystems, deny-by-default networking, scoped mounts, fast startup, suspension, resumption, and predictable scheduling without weakening the security boundary.
Inference systems. Improve the serving systems beneath the Model Gateway, optimizing throughput, latency, accelerator utilization, reliability, and cost. The work is measurement driven: understand the workload, identify the actual bottleneck, and decide where changes to serving, scheduling, caching, model format, or hardware create structural advantage.
Resource scheduling and isolation. Make CPU, memory, storage, network, and accelerator capacity explicit so one workload cannot degrade another. Improve placement, admission control, backpressure, autoscaling, and recovery across deployment environments.
Billing and usage metering. Build the concurrent metering mechanism behind the billing capability, accounting for heterogeneous units such as model tokens and sandbox compute time. It must stay correct when many workloads report concurrently, events arrive late or more than once, and long-running jobs reserve capacity before their final usage is known. This involves idempotent ingestion, atomic reservations, reconciliation, and auditable records.
You will start with one focused problem based on your experience and the team's priorities. The expectation is not broad activity across every domain; it is a substantial improvement in the capability, performance, reliability, or economics of the system you take on.
Tech stack
Go and TypeScript in one Bazel monorepo, with implementation choices driven by the system
Linux, containers, microVMs, filesystems, and networking
Protobuf and gRPC for service contracts
Kubernetes across GCP, AWS, Azure, and on-premises deployments
Terraform and Terragrunt for infrastructure orchestration
PostgreSQL and Redis where durable metadata or coordination requires them
Open-source model serving and accelerator infrastructure
You do not need prior experience with every item. You do need enough systems depth to enter an unfamiliar part of the stack, understand its behavior, and make consequential changes safely.
How we work
We operate with high trust and autonomy in squads of 3 to 4 engineers. A squad owns its roadmap, prioritization, technical decisions, and operation in production. Engineers are expected to find the context they need, ask for input when it improves the outcome, and move work forward without waiting for every next step to be assigned.
We align asynchronously before scheduling a meeting. Product requirement documents (PRDs) define the user problem, intended outcome, and constraints. Design documents make architectural boundaries, tradeoffs, failure modes, migrations, and rollouts explicit. People read and challenge the thinking asynchronously; once the context is shared, a short in-office discussion or whiteboard session usually resolves the remaining questions quickly.
We optimize for leverage. Engineers choose the AI tools that work for them, supported by clear ticket context, focused branches, automated tests, and AI review before human review. We also invest in observability, migration tooling, automated recovery, and runbooks so recurring product maintenance does not depend on someone remembering a manual step.
The engineer who ships a change owns it in production. If something breaks, you lead the fix.

You have owned technically difficult production systems in areas such as distributed systems, databases, runtimes, inference, networking, or storage. You operate what you build and remain responsible for it after deployment.
You reason from first principles, form testable hypotheses, and use measurement to understand unfamiliar behavior. You investigate beyond the first working solution until you understand the underlying mechanism.
Given an underspecified problem, you identify the most important invariant, decide where depth will change the outcome, and defend what you deliberately leave out.
You reason precisely about concurrency, isolation, ordering, data loss, and failure, while finding pragmatic ways to improve performance, reliability, or cost without unnecessary complexity.
You use AI tools as leverage while verifying their output and retaining ownership of the result. You communicate complex systems clearly, expose uncertainty, and work constructively with others.

About Focused Energy
Focused Energy is a pioneering international deep-tech company with locations in Germany and the US, dedicated to commercializing laser-driven nuclear fusion. Our mission is to deliver clean, safe, and virtually limitless energy to the world. As we rapidly scale, we seek talented individuals who thrive on bringing clarity and structure to fast-growing environments.

Focused Energy’s German operations are growing, and the IT systems supporting that growth need an engineer who can own their operation with confidence. As an IT Systems Engineer, you’ll ensure that Focused Energy’s Darmstadt IT environment runs reliably, securely, and efficiently across device management, endpoint security, cloud services, access management, and automation.
This is a systems ownership role, with end-user support as a secondary responsibility. You’ll work onsite in Darmstadt, collaborate with colleagues across Berlin and Austin, and help build a more stable, automated, and scalable IT environment for the scientists and engineers developing fusion technology.

Own the operation and maintenance of IT systems and infrastructure in Darmstadt, including MDM, endpoint security, cloud services, device lifecycle, and access management.
Lead automation and scripting initiatives that reduce repetitive manual work, improve consistency, and increase operational efficiency.
Manage onboarding and offboarding IT execution, including account provisioning, device readiness, access management, and access revocation.
Maintain and improve Focused Energy’s security baseline by supporting MFA enforcement, endpoint hardening, patch management, access reviews, and security event response.
Build and maintain accurate system documentation, configuration records, support processes, and operational runbooks.
Identify recurring incidents and improvement opportunities, investigate root causes, and implement lasting technical solutions.
Contribute to IT improvement projects such as MDM consolidation, cloud service migration, DLP implementation, EDR rollout, and unified device management.
Provide efficient end-user support to Darmstadt employees while coordinating shared infrastructure with the wider IT team and escalating architectural changes, security incidents, and vendor decisions appropriately.

You take ownership of systems issues and improvement opportunities without waiting to be assigned tasks.
You are technically confident, hands-on, and comfortable operating interconnected systems in a fast-growing environment.
You think in systems, considering how components interact before making configuration or production changes.
You are proactive about identifying risks, recurring issues, automation opportunities, and operational improvements.
You communicate system status, incidents, risks, and project progress clearly in English; German language skills are a plus.
You follow through to resolution, document what was changed and why, and work to prevent issues from recurring.
You can balance systems engineering responsibilities with secondary end-user support demands.
You collaborate effectively with employees, People Operations, IT colleagues across sites, vendors, and service providers.
Desirable Skills & Knowledge
Experience in IT systems engineering, including endpoint management, cloud services, identity and access management, and network fundamentals.
Strong experience with MDM platforms and device lifecycle management across Windows and macOS environments.
Practical knowledge of endpoint security, EDR and DLP tooling, endpoint hardening, patch management, and MFA enforcement.
Familiarity with Microsoft 365, including Exchange, Teams, SharePoint, and Intune or an equivalent MDM platform.
Experience with Box, Atlassian tools such as Jira and Confluence, access management platforms, and cloud infrastructure services.
Scripting and automation skills using PowerShell, Python, or an equivalent language.
Knowledge of ITIL-aligned incident and change management, root-cause analysis, and documentation-first operational practices.
Understanding of GDPR requirements applicable to German IT operations and disciplined access review and security procedures.

Axiom is using zero-knowledge proofs to enable new types of verifiable and private software applications, starting with crypto and fintech. We are a small but incredibly strong team backed by the best investors in crypto . We’re looking for exceptional people who are excited to work on challenging and impactful problems in a fast-paced environment. Our office is in NYC and working in person in NY is our strong preference, but we're open to remote candidates as well.
We recently released OpenVM , a performant and modular zkVM framework built for customization and extensibility. OpenVM allows developers to verify the correct execution of arbitrary computer programs in a flexible and performant way. We are building ZK-enabled products using OpenVM and supporting teams building on OpenVM.

We are looking for a distributed systems engineer to join a startup using zero-knowledge proofs to scale smart contract applications. You will be responsible for building Rust-based rollup nodes and sequencers to deliver zero-knowledge proof based products on-chain. Your work will require designing secure and efficient systems and making design choices to enable rapid development without sacrificing security.
We are looking for someone with strong engineering design skills, a security mindset, and the ability to design and implement blockchain protocols. We also value the ability to make pragmatic technology choices which empower our small team.

You are fluent in Rust, C++, or a similarly performant backend language. We work primarily in Rust.
You have experience deploying and monitoring high uptime applications to production in the cloud using orchestration and containerization (Docker, Terraform, Kubernetes).
You have experience working within a large production codebase.
You are extremely detail oriented and have a security mindset.
You’re a clear communicator and value collaboration.
You have a bias towards action and extremely strong work ethic.
Bonuses
You have experience working with blockchain nodes like Geth, Reth, or similar.
You have experience with low-level details of Ethereum.
You have experience working in an adversarial or security critical environment.
You’ll be working on groundbreaking tech that has the potential to be a key piece of infrastructure for the crypto industry

s.h: You’ll receive a competitive salary with equity
s.t:
You will work with and receive mentorship from an exceptional team
Our Team
Our founders Yi Sun and Jonathan Wang met while studying math at Harvard and have been working on ZK since 2021. Together, they wrote some of the most performant ZK circuits for elliptic curve cryptography and Ethereum data reads before starting Axiom.
Before Axiom, Yi was a professor at UChicago Statistics and did a math PhD at MIT. He was previously an advisor for Gauntlet and worked at an HFT startup from inception to profitable trading. Jonathan published number theory research in top math journals and did a math PhD at UChicago.
The rest of our small but incredibly strong team includes alums of Applied Intuition, Coinbase, Color, Neon, Google, and Perplexity as well as math / CS PhDs and IMO / IPhO / Codeforces winners. We look forward to working with you!

We're looking for a Product Integration Engineer to develop and prove out our products with military customers, starting with the Field Operator HUD (FOH): a head-mounted, always-on visual intelligence system built from Distance hardware, a HUD operating system and AI-assisted data processing that pulls sensor, feeds and command-and-control into the operator's field of view.

Your job is to make it work on a specific customer's platform, in the field, not just on a bench, as part of our core R&D team. If you're a hands-on generalist who knows VR or XR and would rather be where the tech meets the user than stuck at a desk, this one's for you.

At Distance Technologies, the problem we're solving is simple to state and hard to solve: the amount of data in the world is endless, but human capacity is not. We are building a fundamentally new perception layer between humans and machines, transforming transparent surfaces into interfaces unlike the world has ever seen.

Think of the windscreen of a car, the visor of a helmet, or a sight device, each becoming a new front-end for AI. The way we turn bits and atoms into expanded human perception is protected by over 50 granted international patent families. We build it for two demanding worlds: defence and automotive.

And we build it from a single foundation fusing software, hardware and computational optics.
There are 60 of us today, with decades-long experience building world's best products, optics, and open-source operating systems. We partner and build with globally leading companies like KIA , Supacat , and Galvion , and we were Google Ventures' first investment in Finland.

The FOH is already in field trials with military users. Your first project is getting it working with British Army equipment and defence primes, building the integration around what the customer actually needs. As our product line grows you'll take on a widening set of customer integrations across our defence work, each one a different platform, stack and set of interfaces.

Owning customer integrations end to end. Make the FOH work inside a customer's platform: adapt the software, wire it into their sensors, displays, video and connectivity, and get it demo- and trial-ready. Prototype fast in dedicated environments to prove value with a client before it hits the shared codebase.
Being Distance in the field. Join demos, trials and exercises with defence clients, support on-site deployments when needed, and bring back what you see and hear on real kit.
Bridging the field and the core. Turn what customers need into concrete integration work with the R&D and commercial teams, spot what should become shared product capability, and feed it into the roadmap and, eventually, the shared codebase.
You won't be a satellite. You'll join the software standups and reviews and be a real part of R&D.

Your work ships and gets used. What you integrate goes into real kit already in trials with military users, and what you learn from demos, trials and exercises with them feeds straight back into the product.
You own the whole thread. From first prototype to working integration in the field, it's yours, not passed between five teams.
New display tech. Glasses-free computational optics and a see-through HUD, the kind of problem you won't find at most XR jobs.
A small team backed to move fast. Around 60 of us, Google Ventures' first investment in Finland, and flat enough that your calls count.

A builder, not a passenger: a hands-on self-starter who takes ownership, works things out when docs are missing, and would rather be with a customer or in the field than at a desk.
At least a couple of years of software engineering experience with VR or XR, plus generalist instincts.
Comfort across a mixed software stack. You've worked with some of C++, Unity and embedded, and you pick up the rest quickly.
Some exposure to electrical integration or software-to-hardware interfaces. We're not expecting deep hardware experience on top of strong software.
You're at home in prototype and integration work: incomplete docs, customer-specific stacks, messy interfaces.
Good with clients, and happy to be the person representing Distance at a demo or trial.
Willing to travel within the UK when needed, and to Finland now and then.
It's a bonus, though not required, if you've worked with HMDs, wearable displays or spatial computing, know C++ for integration and application development, can stand up a UI or application stack for quick situational-awareness or demo prototypes, are comfortable with embedded or Linux at integration level, or have seen sensor, display and video interfaces at system level.

Led by Prof. Dr. Thomas Zurbuchen, ETH Zurich | Space brings together space-related research, education and technology development across ETH Zurich. Working with academic, industrial and institutional partners, the initiative develops new space missions, instruments and technologies.
This position is offered as a fixed-term appointment for an initial period of two years, with the possibility of extension.
Projekthintergrund
The objective of this initiative is to establish and grow a centralized pool of space engineering expertise within ETH Zurich | Space. This pool supports ETH Zurich-led space projects and technology programs, strengthening ETH Zurich’s role in the Swiss and international space ecosystem.
The Flight Software Systems Engineer will support a diverse portfolio of small spacecraft, scientific instruments, robotic systems, and technology demonstrators. The work includes resource-constrained missions, integration with externally supplied spacecraft platforms, autonomous functions, and future distributed or coordinated spacecraft concepts.

This role interfaces across systems engineering, avionics, payloads, and software development, and coordinates with external platform providers and mission operations teams.
Aufgaben-/Stellenbeschreibung
As part of the specialized resource pool, you will provide flight software and software systems engineering expertise across multiple ETH Zurich space projects. You will contribute from early mission formulation and software architecture through implementation, integration, verification, launch preparation, and operations.

s.h: As part of your role, you will
s.t:
Take technical ownership of assigned flight software developments and act as the primary software interface to systems engineering, avionics, payload teams, mission operations, and external platform providers.
Translate mission concept of operations into spacecraft behaviors and define flight software architectures and functional decompositions
Allocate hardware-software functions, and define associated software requirements and interfaces.
Translate mission and system requirements into software specifications, interface control documents, operational concepts, and verification plans.
Develop embedded flight software in C and C++ and supporting tools and test scripts (e.g., Python), including device drivers, telemetry and telecommand handling, onboard data management, application software, and fault-management functions.
Integrate flight software with onboard computers, sensors, actuators, payload electronics, communication interfaces, ground systems, and externally supplied spacecraft platforms.
Set up and maintain flat-sat flight software testbeds
Perform software-related trade studies covering processing capacity, memory, timing, bandwidth, autonomy, reliability, and fault tolerance.
Develop real-time, event-driven, autonomous, synchronization, and GNC-related software functions where required.
Establish and maintain software baselines, configuration control, versioning, build automation, continuous integration, release management, and requirements traceability.
Develop and execute flight software unit tests, conduct integration, software-in-the-loop, processor-in-the-loop, hardware-in-the-loop, and system-level verification and validation activities.
Support software risk management, anomaly investigation, non-conformance handling, and technical review boards.
Support spacecraft and payload assembly, integration, and test activities, commissioning, in-flight software updates, telemetry analysis, and mission operations.
Contribute to technical reviews, early-stage mission concepts, proposals, and software feasibility studies.
Provide technical guidance to junior engineers, researchers, and student teams.
Ihr Profil
You have a strong background in embedded and real-time software development combined with systems-level experience in software architecture, requirements engineering, interface definition, integration, and functional verification. You are comfortable working across mission, spacecraft, avionics, payload, software, and operations domains.

s.h: We are looking for someone with
s.t:
Master’s degree in computer science, electrical engineering, computer engineering, aerospace engineering, robotics, or a related field.
5+ years of professional experience in flight software, embedded software, or mission-critical software systems.
Strong programming skills in C and C++ for resource-constrained embedded targets.
Experience with real-time operating systems, embedded Linux, or bare-metal development.
Experience in software systems engineering, including architecture definition, functional decomposition, hardware-software allocation, requirements management, and interface control.
Ability to translate mission and spacecraft requirements into software specifications, operational concepts, and verification strategies.
Experience integrating flight software with avionics hardware, sensors, actuators, communication buses, payloads, or ground systems.
Understanding of telemetry and telecommand, onboard data handling, timing, autonomy, fault management, and spacecraft operations.
Hands-on experience with software integration, debugging, automated testing, and hardware-in-the-loop environments.
Experience with configuration management, version control, release processes, technical baselines, and requirements traceability.
Ability to assess software-related technical resources, including processing capacity, memory, timing, bandwidth, and reliability margins.
Strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills, with the ability to work effectively in multidisciplinary and multicultural teams.
Knowledge of radiation effects, redundancy, memory protection, watchdogs, and FDIR.
Excellent command of English, both written and spoken; German is an advantage but not required.

s.h: Additionally, the following characteristics are a plus
s.t:
Experience developing flight software for CubeSats, small satellites, scientific instruments, planetary systems, or Class D/Gamma-type missions.
Experience leading or coordinating software-related and functional AIT activities, including test planning, execution, anomaly resolution, and system-level functional verification.
Experience integrating payload software with spacecraft platforms supplied by external industrial partners.
Familiarity with ECSS software engineering and software product assurance standards, NASA software practices, or comparable development frameworks.
Experience with spacecraft protocols and buses such as SpaceWire, CAN, UART, SPI, I²C, Ethernet, or CCSDS-based services.
Experience with flight software frameworks or operating systems such as NASA cFS, F Prime, RTEMS, FreeRTOS, Zephyr, or equivalent.
Experience with autonomous systems, robotic software, relative navigation, formation flying, or distributed spacecraft coordination.
Experience with FPGA or firmware interfaces and hardware-software co-design.
Experience with EGSE, simulators, ground software, commissioning, or in-orbit operations.
Experience collaborating with international partners, space agencies, research institutions, or spacecraft suppliers.
